title: Paying the sources: a simulation
summary: How the money a reader spends on PrompTugal.news would be shared with the outlets, writers, public bodies and data providers behind what they read. A simulation: no money moves.

intro: PrompTugal.news is built on other people's work: outlets, writers, public bodies and data providers. Dinis asked how the money readers spend here would be shared with them. Nothing is paid yet; this page simulates it, with every assumption shown.

**The model.** Revenue comes in (a reader's spend; later, traffic). A share is kept for costs. The rest is split across the sources behind the pages that were read, by the weight of what each source gave the page. A source is paid only once its share passes a minimum; until then it carries over.
How much is kept, the weights, the minimum and when anyone is paid are Dinis's to decide. When it becomes real, it becomes a decision page for him first.
mine_about: Worked out in this browser from the reading log the meter already keeps on your device. Nothing about you or what you read is sent to us.
mine_no_js: This part needs JavaScript: it reads your reading log on your device and never sends it.
mine_empty: No pages in this browser's reading log yet, or none with sources we can see. Read a few articles or place pages and come back.
ledger_heading: The ledger: every source, every page
ledger_about: From the links and source fields the pages already carry, counted at each release. Appearances: pages that use the source. Weight: the sum of what it gave them. Page-view counts join when the anonymous counts are published.
how: Articles: every link to an outside site is a cited fact; a link inside a quotation counts as quoted words. Images and our own sites are left out.
Place pages: every story or listing's source is discovery evidence; the live weather and flights are data sets.

A source is the site's host name (an outlet, a blog, a public body, a data provider). Where one person publishes on a shared platform, they are counted under the platform until the register names them.
The full ledger is open data: [api/v1/payments/attribution.json](../../api/v1/payments/attribution.json).

The data site keeps its own side, for the data sets it collects (data.b@, also simulated): [data.promptugal.news/api/v1/sources/attribution.json](https://data.promptugal.news/api/v1/sources/attribution.json). Its weights are its own assumption (appearances plus twice the citations); the two ledgers are shown side by side, not added, until Dinis settles one model.
api_about: The simulated attribution ledger of promptugal.news: for each page (by its address, as the meter logs it), the outside sources behind it with their weights; and per source its appearances and weight. A simulation: no money moves.
